claims: A variable is a name that refers to a stored value; the assignment operator = binds the name on the left to the value produced on the right (for objects it binds the reference, so no copy is made).
A statement sets a variable to a value using the assignment operator (=), with the name on the left and the value on the right.
Assignment is not mathematical equality — = copies a value into a variable rather than asserting two sides are equal.
A variable name may contain letters, digits, and underscores and be any length, but cannot start with a digit.
Variable names are case-sensitive, so total and Total are two different variables.

anchors.quote: Variables allow programs to refer to values using names rather than memory locations
A statement can set a variable to a value using the assignment operator (=)
Note that this is different from the equal sign of mathematics
A variable name can consist of letters, digits, and underscores and be of any length
